recognize_zh: 大多數紅血球的中央淡染區不是圓形，而是一條細長像嘴巴或裂縫的蒼白帶（slit-like central pallor），整片均勻出現，這就是口形紅血球（stomatocyte）。
features: Normocytic red cells, the majority showing a linear, slit- or mouth-like central pallor (stomatocytes)
Occasional cells with round central pallor and rare target-like forms
No significant spherocytes, schistocytes or red cell inclusions evident
Segmented neutrophil with normal granulation (lower right)
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a red cell population dominated by stomatocytes, with a linear slit-like central pallor replacing the normal round pallor in most cells. Red cells are otherwise fairly uniform in size, without significant spherocytes, schistocytes or nucleated red cells in this field. Platelets appear adequate and the neutrophil seen is morphologically unremarkable. Findings are consistent with stomatocytosis; in this clinical setting (severe COVID-19 with liver injury) an acquired cause is favored, but the possibility of drying artifact should be excluded by confirming the finding in well-spread areas of a fresh smear.

ddx.vs: Artifactual stomatocytes are confined to thick parts of the smear, whereas true stomatocytosis is present uniformly in the thin monolayer.
Hereditary forms show chronic compensated hemolysis, abnormal MCHC and osmotic gradient ektacytometry, and family history rather than an acquired transient pattern.
SAO cells are oval with one or two transverse slits or bars rather than round cells with a single mouth-like pallor.
Target cells have a central dense hemoglobin spot surrounded by a pale ring, not a linear slit.
